events.continuity_hook: Begins a new work-travel episode after the Colorado trip wraps up.
events.interaction_goal: Frame the Raleigh-Durham trip, identify workable flight windows and hotel areas, and list what Maya needs from the client before routing anything for approval.
events.scenario_brief: After returning from the Colorado family trip, Maya receives a new client-site request in the Raleigh-Durham area for Monday, August 18 through Thursday, August 21. The client expects a Tuesday morning kickoff, but the exact office building is still listed only as a Durham medical-campus location. She wants to fly from Atlanta after her Monday internal call, return Thursday afternoon if the wrap-up ends on time, avoid a fussy connection, and find a hotel with strong guest ratings, short rideshares, breakfast if practical, and dinner options nearby. The unresolved items are the exact street address and the Thursday end time.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the Raleigh-Durham work trip now that the office area is clearer but the return-day timing is not.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the flight-and-hotel packages, call out the breakfast versus commute tradeoff, and decide which option is strongest for approval.
events.scenario_brief: The client confirms a downtown Durham medical-office address and an 8:30 a.m. Tuesday start. Maya is comparing a Monday evening Delta nonstop that reaches RDU around dinner with a cheaper one-stop itinerary that arrives much later and adds connection risk. Hotel choices now center on a closer downtown business hotel with very good recent reviews and an on-site restaurant but paid breakfast, versus a suite-style property with breakfast near RTP that would mean longer rideshares each morning. Thursday's debrief is still shown as late morning without a firm finish time.

events.continuity_hook: Keeps the Raleigh-Durham episode moving after approval, with a return-flight timing issue introduced by the client agenda.
events.interaction_goal: Compare keeping the original return against moving to the later nonstop, and identify the one agenda detail Maya should ask the client to firm up before changing the ticket.
events.scenario_brief: Maya's manager approves the Raleigh-Durham trip, including the closer downtown hotel as long as the cancellable rate stays in range. A client agenda update now shows the Thursday wrap-up may run until about 1:30 p.m., making the mid-afternoon RDU-to-Atlanta return tighter than it looked at first. A later Delta nonstop is still available but gets her home noticeably later, and the one-stop options do not save enough to be attractive. The hotel is unaffected, but she needs to decide whether to change the return before the fare difference grows.

events.continuity_hook: Final pre-departure pass for the Raleigh-Durham work trip after the return-flight risk is resolved.
events.interaction_goal: Confirm the keep-as-booked plan and leave Maya with a concise travel-day and hotel-arrival checklist.
events.scenario_brief: A few days before departure, the client clarifies that Thursday's wrap-up should finish before lunch, so Maya plans to keep the original afternoon return. She wants a final rundown covering Atlanta airport timing, the RDU arrival transfer to the Durham hotel, check-in timing, nearby dinner choices for Monday night, the hotel's breakfast status, and whether any window seat has opened on either leg. The only remaining hotel detail is whether to request a quiet room in advance or wait until arrival.

events.continuity_hook: Starts a new family leisure episode after a run of work travel.
events.interaction_goal: Narrow the Gulf Coast destination options, outline flight windows from Atlanta, and define the hotel features that matter most for the family weekend.
events.scenario_brief: With the Raleigh-Durham trip completed, Maya starts looking at a short family fall-break beach trip for Friday, October 10 through Monday, October 13. Her spouse is leaning toward the Gulf Coast, with Tampa or Sarasota as possible arrival airports, and they want a hotel or condo-style property close enough to reach the beach easily without making every day car-dependent. They need room for two adults and one child, a pool would help, breakfast would simplify mornings, and she wants to avoid a late return that would make the school-night reset harder. The unresolved choices are which airport makes the cleanest flight schedule and whether they should rent a car.

events.continuity_hook: Continues the fall-break family trip after the destination area is narrowed.
events.interaction_goal: Compare the two flight-and-lodging packages, weigh beach access against breakfast and parking costs, and decide what to place on a cancellable hold.
events.scenario_brief: The family narrows the fall-break trip to the St. Pete Beach area. Maya is comparing a Friday afternoon Atlanta-to-Tampa nonstop with a cheaper Saturday morning departure, and she prefers a Monday afternoon return if the price difference is reasonable. The top lodging choices are a beach-block property with strong reviews, parking fees, and no included breakfast, versus an inland suite-style hotel with breakfast and easier parking but a daily drive or rideshare to the beach. The open question is whether paying more for walkable beach access is worth avoiding a rental car for the weekend.
